To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
FAD binds to the flavin-binding site of Fre much more tightly than riboflavin or FMN and that FAD is not an obligatory cofactor for Fre.
FAD is an unusual substrate for Fre and that it is an inhibitor at low NAD(P) H concentrations.
the binding of FAD to Fre is much tighter than that of riboflavin or FMN, that FAD and NAPD(P)H share a binding site, and that FAD is both an inhibitor and a preferred substrate for Fre.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the binding of FAD to the enzyme and its effect on the catalytic properties of Fre, which is a key enzyme in the bacterial metabolism of flavins and flavin nucleotides.
the interaction of Fre with FAD, which may be of physiological relevance in the reduction of FAD by NAD(P) H.
the mechanism of the flavin cofactors binding to Fre and the effect of this binding on the enzyme activity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the overlapping binding of NAD(P) and FMN/FAD to Fre is a major factor that determines the kinetic behavior of this flavin-dependent NAD(P) oxidoreductase.
the overlapping of the FAD- and NAD(P)(H)-binding sites is a key feature of Fre, and that it has a profound influence on the kinetic properties of Fre.
FAD is an inhibitor of Fre, which reduces it preferentially to riboflavin, but not FMN.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Fre has evolved to reduce FAD in preference to FMN and to reduce FMN in preference to riboflavin.
the binding of FAD to Fre is more favorable energetically and kinetically than that of FMN, which in turn is more favorable than that of riboflavin.
the binding of FAD to Fre is more than just a passive binding of a substrate; it is an active process that leads to the formation of a unique FAD·Fre complex.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the flavin-binding site of Fre is a flexible binding pocket that accommodates the isoalloxazines of FAD and FMN, with the isoalloxazinyl ring being the primary determinant of the binding.

the flavin substrate of Fre binds to the enzyme mainly through its isoalloxazine moiety, with the ribityl side chains and ADP moieties of FAD and FMN contributing additional interactions with the enzyme.
the overlapping binding sites may have a significant effect on the catalytic properties of Fre.
